label: Retained readings from Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae
summary: I q.10 a.3 co. and ad 2: aeternitas vere et proprie in solo Deo est: The participated-eternity definition cites the distinction between proper and participated or extended eternity. The case's operational duration calibration needs an explicit test for that distinction on the same bearer before the exclusive scope of proper eternity can enter the route. I q.14 a.4 co.: The existing intellect attempt 627f23ba compares the identity of divine understanding and esse. The possession-of-intellect and operation premises do not themselves assert that identity. The open bridge must identify the understanding exercise with esse of the same divine bearer. I q.2 a.3 co., quinta via: et hoc dicimus Deum: The Fifth Way applies the name God to its intelligent director of natural things. This is sourced usage in the GOD_3 definition. The case’s full-profile naming premise would still need the director to meet its whole description and the application of the name to be carried by that same witness. I q.2 a.3 co., secunda via: quam omnes Deum nominant: The Second Way reports that everyone names its first efficient cause God. This is sourced usage in the GOD_3 definition. Its connection to the full-profile premise needs the first efficient cause to be the witness of that profile. The wording supplies no identity with the Fifth Way director. I q.85 a.1 ad 2 [32018]: quantitates, ut numeri et dimensiones et figurae ... possunt considerari absque qualitatibus sensibilibus ... Plato ... omnia quae diximus abstrahi per intellectum, posuit abstracta esse secundum rem: The concrete–abstract comparison uses this claim about intellectual abstraction in docs/notes/concrete-abstract.md. The case partition needs a bridge from separation in thought to whether a value has the relevant esse in re. Intellectual consideration apart from sensible qualities does not supply that bridge. I-II q.94 a.2 co.: Secundum se quidem quaelibet propositio dicitur per se nota, cuius praedicatum est de ratione subiecti; contingit tamen quod ignoranti definitionem subiecti, talis propositio non erit per se nota: The natural-law per se nota definition uses this account of self-evidence in itself and its distinction from self-evidence to a knower. Applying it to a particular case-floor item needs an analysis of its subject account and a reason that its predicate belongs to it.
